name: São Tomé and Príncipe
official: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe

facts.religion: Catholic about 55%, Protestant and other Christian

snapshot: Two cocoa islands in the Gulf of Guinea that voted twice in 2026: President Carlos Vila Nova won a second term in July, and the opposition MLSTP topped September's parliamentary election without a majority.
culture: The uninhabited islands were settled by the Portuguese with enslaved Africans to grow sugar, and later cocoa on vast plantations called roças, many now crumbling or turned into hotels. Forro and other creoles are spoken alongside Portuguese. The Tchiloli, a 16th-century European drama performed in masks and costume, has become a uniquely São Toméan art form.
society: Cocoa remains the main export, and tourism is growing slowly. The state relies heavily on foreign aid. Hopes of offshore oil have repeatedly faded. Political rivalry is intense: President Carlos Vila Nova sacked Prime Minister Patrice Trovoada in January 2025.
situation: After President Carlos Vila Nova dismissed Prime Minister Patrice Trovoada in January 2025, he appointed Américo Ramos. In July 2026 Vila Nova won re-election in a peaceful vote with historically low turnout. In the 27 September parliamentary election the MLSTP came first with 24 of 55 seats, short of a majority, setting up coalition talks to choose the next government. A 2022 attack on the army headquarters, in which detainees were killed in custody, still shapes politics.
power: A semi-presidential republic. The president is directly elected for five years and appoints the prime minister, who must hold the confidence of the 55-seat National Assembly.

leaders.state: President Carlos Vila Nova, re-elected July 2026
leaders.gov: Prime Minister Américo Ramos, pending a new government after the September 2026 election
